Maya (Finance): Heads-up — ACME Inc just uploaded invoice 3310 for RD-EU-001 but it's missing the reverse-charge wording and doesn't show our VAT ID. They left VAT at 0% but no note.
Liam (Accounting): Ugh. Can you paste the invoice PDF name or snippet? We need to decide whether to pay or query.
Maya (Finance): Filename: ACME_3310_2026-03.pdf
Maya (Finance): Snippet: `Supplier VAT: 00-0000000; Tax: 0%` — no reverse-charge line and no customer VAT ID.
Elena (Tax): If it's intercompany / cross-border service to our EU entity we need either: vendor to add "reverse charge — VAT to be accounted by the recipient" + our VAT ID, OR evidence they applied correct local tax treatment. Otherwise risk reclaim/refund issues.
Victor (VendorOps): Pinged ACME: "Please re-issue invoice with reverse-charge statement and include Redwood EU VAT ID RD-EU-001. If they insist they charged 0% we need confirmation of their legal basis"
Sam (Billing): Also FYI vendor asked about grossing-up payments if withholdings apply — are we expecting any US withholding on this one?
Elena (Tax): For service fees between a US supplier and an EU company, withholding typically depends on the type of service and tax treaties. For standard SaaS-like fees, often no US withholding if paid to a US corp; but if they request gross-up we need W-8/W-9 docs to determine.
Maya (Finance): ACME asked whether we can accept W-9 or W-8BEN-E. I told them I wasn't sure which we need for an EU entity.
Elena (Tax): For our EU legal entity, we should have W-8 BEN-E on file from a non-US payee? Wait — ACME is US-based, so they'd provide W-9 if they are US persons. If they're asking for our W-8, that's backwards. We should send them our EU VAT details and a contact for tax residency evidence.
Victor (VendorOps): ACME replied: "We're US tax residents, we can provide W-9. We charged 0% VAT assuming exported services; will reissue with reverse charge note and include your VAT ID if you confirm."
Liam (Accounting): OK — steps: 1) Confirm our VAT ID to ACME (RD-EU-001) 2) Ask ACME to reissue with reverse-charge line and that exact VAT ID 3) Request their W-9 for our records (since they're US). 4) Hold payment until invoice corrected? Thoughts.
Elena (Tax): Agree hold payment until corrected invoice received. Also save the email trail and W-9 in tax folder for audit. If they insist on gross-up, ask for legal justification and run through tax to confirm whether treaty applies.
Maya (Finance): I'll tell Victor to pause the payment run and share the vendor response thread.
Victor (VendorOps): Payment paused. I've asked ACME to send corrected invoice + W-9. Will post here when they reply. :thumbsup:
invoices-bot: Invoice 3310 (ACME) uploaded by Victor — status: flagged (missing VAT details).
